items.title: In-Distribution Forcing for Long Video Generation at Test Time
items.summary: Modern autoregressive (AR) video diffusion models excel at short-horizon video generation, yet generating long videos remains challenging due to drifting, where colors and textures shift, and motion dynamics decay. items.title: LMBuild: Evaluating LLM Agents for Generating Buildable and Functional Structures
items.summary: LLM-based agents are increasingly capable of generating complex 3D structures, with the potential to reshape how objects are designed and realized in the physical world. items.title: Foundations of Proactive Agents: Principles, Technical Layers, and Proactivity-Gym
items.summary: Proactive LLM agents can turn idle compute into useful support before users ask. Yet even correct work can misread user context, impose review costs, or undermine trust. items.summary: Test-time training (TTT) lets a model store information in its weights during inference. items.title: Optimizing the Optimizer: Language Models Discover Faster Molecular Relaxation
items.summary: Geometry optimization is a major cost in many quantum-chemical workflows: each optimization step requires one force evaluation, and at the density-functional level that evaluation dominates the wall time. items.title: Data Unlearning via Inverse Distillation
items.summary: Multi-step matching models, including flow and diffusion models, produce high-quality outputs but incur substantial inference costs and may reproduce unwanted components of their training datasets. We introduce Inverse Distillation Unlearning (IDU), a unified framework that simultaneously distills a teacher multi-step matching model into an efficient one-step student generator and suppresses outputs corresponding to a designated training subset.

items.title: SearchJev: A Fast and Calibrated System-1 Model for Search Agents
items.summary: Search agents repeatedly make short decisions about relevance, evidence sufficiency, and search actions. Using generative language models for these decisions introduces latency and unreliable confidence. items.summary: We introduce a post-training method for diffusion language models (DLMs) that minimizes Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) between generated and reference distributions in the feature space of a frozen pretrained DLM. items.title: OmniReasoning: Pushing the Limits of Audio-Visual Joint Reasoning
items.summary: Recent advances have enabled unified omni-modal models in understanding audio, vision, and language. However, existing benchmarks, training data, and learning methods largely treat the modalities independently, leaving the capability of audio-visual joint reasoning poorly evaluated and insufficiently elicited. items.title: RobotUse: Allocating Computation, Context, and Decisions
items.summary: Robot agents must connect their intended actions to observed outcomes while retaining the context needed to revise their choices over repeated attempts. Existing interfaces often leave these choices inside predefined tools or require agents to manage detailed execution code and its growing history. items.title: UndoBench: Separating Task Competence from Recovery Capability in Tool-Using AI Agents
items.summary: Tool-using AI agents are increasingly deployed across enterprise software systems, yet widely used benchmarks primarily evaluate nominal task completion, conflating baseline planning competence with operational fault recovery. items.summary: A vision--language--action (VLA) policy can complete complex tasks while ignoring the evidence that should determine its actions. An object held near the wrist camera can displace the instructed target. items.title: World Editing: Intervening on Executable Worlds at Increasing Depth
items.summary: Interactive world models are increasingly capable of generating environments and acting within them, yet deliberately editing an existing executable world remains underexplored. items.summary: Large language models are strong general-purpose code generators, but executable algorithmic trading remains a demanding specialization target: a model must translate a natural-language strategy specification into correct program logic for a specialized trading framework, execute on historical data, produce trades, and remain semantically faithful to the request. items.title: DeskForge: Dense Supervision from Desktop Environments for Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: Computer-use agents need to reliably ground action targets in complex desktop scenes, where multiple applications, overlapping windows, and visually similar controls compete for attention. items.summary: We introduce Loop Flow Transformers (LiFT), a family of looped generative models that scales computation by repeatedly applying a shared Diffusion Transformer (DiT) core, with only light changes to the standard architecture. items.summary: Looped Transformers reuse one block of layers several times: by spending extra computation they push a model of fixed size further, and so use its parameters more fully; while sparse mixture-of-experts (MoE) models activate only a few of many experts for each token. items.title: What Matters for Latent Reasoning with Flow Matching
items.summary: Latent reasoning lets a large language model (LLM) think in a continuous space and verbalize only the answer. items.title: What Gradients Add to Text Leakage in Split Language Models, Counted per Token and per Document
items.summary: Split learning lets a client train a language model on a server without sending its text. items.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly rely on persistent external sources to solve sequences of knowledge-intensive tasks. items.summary: Modern information systems, including many agentic workflows, use dense retrieval to explore large amounts of unstructured data.
